alignments.note: The verbless clause supplies the whole frame *have I to do with* around the dative pronoun, as rule 75 gives *have I to do* to the dative of Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί; rule 17 heads on *I*, the word realizing the pronoun's own lexeme, the supplied frame riding as helpers.
The article's modifier is a bare adverb with no verb to carry a relativizer, so the article keeps *them that* under rule 31, headed on the nominal word.
The adverbial predicate takes the supplied copula under rules 31 and 53, headed on the adverb.
κρίνετε → *Do … judge*, the do-support auxiliary riding with the verb under rule 9 and the head on the lexical verb, discontinuously under rule 15.
οὐχί carries content of its own and is aligned to *not* in the ordinary way under rule 64.
Article with a bare adverb keeps *them that* under rule 31, analysed as its parallel earlier in the verse (rule 24).
The adverbial predicate takes the supplied copula under rule 53.

review_notes: Both τοὺς + adverb phrases are analysed alike under rule 31, the article keeping *them that* and the adverb taking the copula.
The supplied *have … to do with* is folded onto μοι under rule 75, headed on *I* per rule 17.
